description: The planets are treated as worlds with histories: the rocky inner planets, Jupiter, Saturn and the distant ice worlds are reconstructed through the forces and accidents that shaped them.

s04e01.description: Brian traces the divergent histories of Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars, four rocky planets born together but transformed into radically different worlds.

s04e02.description: Brian examines how early Mars and Earth once resembled two blue planets before their climates and prospects for life followed very different paths.

s04e03.description: Brian explores Jupiter, the solar system’s oldest giant, and how its immense gravity shaped the development and survival of worlds around it.

s04e04.description: Brian reconstructs Saturn’s history, from its formation as an ice-and-rock world to a gas giant surrounded by its distinctive rings and moons.

s04e05.description: Brian journeys to Uranus, Neptune and Pluto, the remote ice worlds whose storms, moons and histories were revealed by rare spacecraft encounters.
